newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to present privatisation programme soon.
newsitem.headline: Israel to present privatisation programme soon.

text.p: The Government Corporations Authority will soon present to the Israeli cabinet its privatisation programme for the coming year, Tzippi Livni, the head of the authority, said on Monday.
Livni told reporters that the programme's "top priority will be to disburse as many shares as possible among the public".
She said the most natural way to do this would be to sell shares on the bourse. Companies that are too big to be privatised on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange will be sold on markets abroad, she said.
She said selling shares on the bourse would help to revitalise the ailing Tel Aviv market, adding that the government was committed to this goal, even if the profits from such sales were small.
"There will be no sales that are not in line with the values of companies but the size of the cheque will not be our main consideration in selling companies," she said.

Livni would not say when the programme would be unveiled, though Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said it would be presented in November. Livni also declined to say how many companies would be included in the first year of the programme.
She said it would not include plans developed by the previous Labour government to distribute options to the public to buy shares in state companies at a discount.
"Our programme does not relate to the options programme," she said.
